items.vi: Một quyết định khó khăn
items.p: Tell me about a difficult decision you made. What was the situation? What did you decide, and why? Was it the right decision?
items.pv: Kể về một quyết định khó: hoàn cảnh, bạn chọn gì, vì sao, có đúng không.
u: A few years ago, I had to decide whether to
Vài năm trước tôi phải quyết định có nên
In the end, I decided to
items.m: A few years ago, I had to decide whether to stay in my home town or move to Hanoi for a new job. My parents wanted me to stay, because I am their only son. In the end, I decided to move. The main reason was that the job offered much better training and a higher salary. It was hard at first, because I felt lonely and I missed my family. Looking back, I think it was the right decision. I have learned a lot, and now I visit my parents every month.

items.vi: Công việc lý tưởng
items.p: Describe your ideal job. What would you do? Where would you work? Why would this job suit you?
items.pv: Tả công việc mơ ước: làm gì, ở đâu, vì sao hợp với bạn.
c: Cần làm gì để có việc đó
u: Công việc lý tưởng của tôi sẽ là
To get this job, I would need to
Để có việc này, tôi cần
items.m: My ideal job would be a travel writer. I would work for a magazine or a website, and I would travel to different countries to write about food and culture. I wouldn't need to sit in an office all day. It would suit me because I love meeting new people and I enjoy writing. I'm also quite organised, which is important when you travel a lot. To get this job, I would need to improve my English and build a good portfolio of articles.

items.vi: Công nghệ trong cuộc sống
items.p: How do you use technology in your daily life? What are the advantages and disadvantages? Could you live without your phone for a week?
items.pv: Bạn dùng công nghệ hằng ngày thế nào? Lợi, hại? Sống một tuần không điện thoại được không?
c: Bạn dùng công nghệ làm gì
u: Tôi không nghĩ tôi có thể
items.m: I use my phone for almost everything: to check the news, to message my friends, to pay for things and to learn English. One advantage is that I can find information very quickly. It also helps me stay in touch with my family. On the other hand, I spend too much time on social media, and sometimes I can't sleep because I look at my phone late at night. I don't think I could live without my phone for a week, but maybe I could try for a weekend.

items.vi: Một nơi bạn giới thiệu
items.p: Recommend a place in your country that visitors should see. Where is it? What can people do there? When is the best time to go?
items.pv: Giới thiệu một nơi nên đến ở nước bạn: ở đâu, làm gì, đi lúc nào.
u: The best time to go is
Thời điểm đẹp nhất để đi là
items.m: I'd recommend visiting Ninh Binh, which is located about two hours south of Hanoi. It's famous for its limestone mountains and rice fields. You can take a small boat along the river through caves, ride a bike through the villages or climb to the top of Mua Cave for an amazing view. The best time to go is in late May or early June, when the rice fields turn golden. My advice is to stay at least one night, because it's very peaceful in the evening.

items.vi: Thành phố hay nông thôn
items.p: Some people think life is better in the countryside than in the city. Do you agree? Give reasons and examples, and consider the other point of view.
items.pv: Có người cho rằng sống ở nông thôn tốt hơn thành phố. Bạn đồng ý không? Nêu lý do, ví dụ và xét cả ý ngược lại.
u: Cân nhắc lại, tôi cho rằng
items.m: In my opinion, it depends on your stage of life, but on the whole I prefer the city. For young people especially, cities offer far more opportunities: better jobs, universities and a wider range of cultural activities. For example, in Ho Chi Minh City I can go to concerts, try food from all over the world and meet people from many backgrounds. Having said that, I understand why many people prefer the countryside. The air is cleaner, life is less stressful and housing is much cheaper. Many of my friends with young children have moved back to their home towns for exactly these reasons. On balance, I'd say the city is better for building a career, but the countryside may be better for raising a family.

items.vi: Người ảnh hưởng tới bạn
items.p: Talk about a person who has had a strong influence on your life. Who are they? How did you meet them? In what ways did they change you?
items.pv: Kể về một người ảnh hưởng lớn tới bạn: là ai, gặp thế nào, thay đổi bạn ra sao.
u: The person who has influenced me most is
Người ảnh hưởng tới tôi nhiều nhất là
Lần đầu tôi gặp cô ấy khi
Điều tôi ngưỡng mộ nhất là
items.m: The person who has influenced me most is my high school maths teacher, Mr Quang. I first met him when I was fifteen, at a time when I was failing maths and had almost given up. Instead of criticising me, he stayed after class twice a week to help me, and he always explained things in several different ways until I understood. What I admire most is his patience. He never made me feel stupid. Thanks to him, I not only passed my exams, but I also learned that being bad at something is not permanent. That idea has helped me in everything I've done since, including learning English.

items.vi: Học trực tuyến
items.p: What are the advantages and disadvantages of learning online compared with learning in a classroom? Which do you prefer, and why?
items.pv: So sánh học trực tuyến và học trên lớp: lợi, hại. Bạn thích cách nào, vì sao?
c: Bạn chọn gì và vì sao
u: One clear advantage of online learning is
Một ưu điểm rõ của học trực tuyến là
items.m: One clear advantage of online learning is flexibility. You can study whenever and wherever you like, which is ideal for people who work full-time. It's also usually cheaper, and you can replay lessons as many times as you need. The main drawback is that it's easy to lose motivation when nobody is checking on you. It can also feel quite lonely. In a classroom, by contrast, you can ask questions immediately, practise speaking with other students and get instant feedback from the teacher. Personally, I'd choose a mix of both. I'd use online lessons for grammar and vocabulary, but I'd want a real class for speaking practice, because that's where I need most help.

items.vi: Một sự kiện đáng nhớ
items.p: Describe an event that you will never forget. What happened? Who was there? Why was it so memorable?
items.pv: Kể về một sự kiện bạn không bao giờ quên: chuyện gì, có ai, vì sao đáng nhớ.
u: One event I'll never forget is
Một sự kiện tôi sẽ không bao giờ quên là
items.m: One event I'll never forget is my sister's wedding three years ago. It all started badly: on the morning of the wedding, there was a huge storm and the power went off in the whole street. The make-up artist couldn't see anything, and my sister was close to tears. To my surprise, all our neighbours came out with torches and candles to help. By the afternoon the sun came out, and the ceremony in the garden was beautiful. My whole family was there, including my grandmother, who had travelled from the countryside. It was memorable because it showed me how a community can turn a disaster into something wonderful.

items.vi: Đại học có nên miễn phí?
items.p: Some people argue that university education should be free for everyone. Discuss the arguments for and against, and give your own view.
items.pv: Có ý kiến cho rằng đại học nên miễn phí cho mọi người. Bàn ý ủng hộ, phản đối và nêu quan điểm.
u: Người ủng hộ lập luận rằng
Tuy nhiên, người phản đối chỉ ra rằng
Một giải pháp dung hoà có thể là
items.m: Proponents argue that free university education is a matter of fairness. Talent is spread evenly across society, but money is not, so charging fees means that many capable young people from poor families never get the chance to study. A more educated population also benefits the whole economy. Critics, however, point out that someone has to pay, and that free tuition often benefits middle-class families most, since their children are more likely to go to university anyway. There is also a risk that universities become underfunded and overcrowded. My own view is that cost should never be the reason a talented student cannot study. A compromise might be to make university free for students from lower-income families, while others repay loans once they earn above a certain salary.

items.vi: Tác động của mạng xã hội
items.p: How has social media changed the way people communicate and form opinions? Is the overall effect positive or negative?
items.pv: Mạng xã hội đã thay đổi cách con người giao tiếp và hình thành quan điểm ra sao? Tác động chung là tích cực hay tiêu cực?
c: Ảnh hưởng tới cách hình thành quan điểm
u: Mạng xã hội đã thay đổi căn bản
items.m: Social media has fundamentally changed how we communicate. We now stay in constant contact with hundreds of people, including many we have never met, and news travels in seconds rather than days. One consequence is that our opinions are increasingly shaped by algorithms that show us content we already agree with. This can create echo chambers, where people rarely encounter opposing views and become more extreme. Misinformation also spreads faster than corrections. That said, social media has undeniable benefits. It has given a voice to people who were previously ignored, helped small businesses reach customers and allowed communities to organise quickly in emergencies. Overall, I'd argue that the effect is mixed, and that it depends largely on how critically we use it.

items.vi: Cân bằng công việc và cuộc sống
items.p: Many people say it is increasingly difficult to achieve a healthy work-life balance. Why might this be? What can individuals and employers do about it?
items.pv: Nhiều người nói ngày càng khó cân bằng công việc và cuộc sống. Vì sao? Cá nhân và công ty có thể làm gì?
c: Cá nhân có thể làm gì
Công ty có thể làm gì
u: There are several reasons for this.
Có vài lý do cho điều này.
items.m: There are several reasons for this. Technology means that many of us are reachable at any time, so the working day never truly ends. Economic pressure and job insecurity also push people to work longer hours to prove their value. As a result, stress and burnout have become extremely common, and relationships and health often suffer. On a personal level, people can set clear boundaries, for example by switching off work notifications in the evening and protecting time for exercise and family. Employers, for their part, have a responsibility too. They can discourage emails outside working hours, offer flexible schedules and, most importantly, ensure that managers lead by example, since staff tend to copy what their bosses do rather than what they say.

items.vi: Gìn giữ truyền thống
items.p: In a globalised world, is it important to preserve traditional customs and crafts? Who should be responsible for this?
items.pv: Trong thế giới toàn cầu hoá, có cần giữ phong tục, nghề truyền thống? Ai nên chịu trách nhiệm?
c: Quan điểm: có quan trọng không
Lý do, ví dụ cụ thể
u: I'd argue that it is essential to
The difficulty, of course, is that
Trách nhiệm nên được chia giữa
items.m: I'd argue that it is essential to preserve traditional customs and crafts, not because the past is always better, but because they give communities a sense of identity and continuity. Take, for instance, the pottery village of Bat Trang. Its techniques have been passed down for centuries, and losing them would mean losing knowledge that cannot be recovered. The difficulty, of course, is that young people often see little future in traditional crafts, which tend to be poorly paid compared with factory or office work. Responsibility should be shared between governments, which can provide funding and protect heritage sites, and communities themselves, who can find ways to make traditions relevant today, for example through tourism, design collaborations or online sales.

items.vi: Tiến bộ có luôn tốt?
items.p: "Not all progress is improvement." Discuss this statement with reference to technology, society or the environment.
items.pv: “Không phải tiến bộ nào cũng là cải thiện.” Bàn về nhận định này, liên hệ công nghệ, xã hội hoặc môi trường.
c: Ví dụ tiến bộ có cái giá
u: At first glance, the statement seems
Thoạt nhìn, nhận định có vẻ
It would be simplistic, however, to
Tuy nhiên sẽ là quá đơn giản nếu
Ultimately, the question is not whether … but
Rốt cuộc, câu hỏi không phải là … mà là
items.m: At first glance, the statement seems almost paradoxical, since we tend to use 'progress' as a synonym for improvement. But progress, strictly speaking, simply means movement in a particular direction, and whether that direction is desirable is a separate question. A telling example is the rise of the car. It brought unprecedented freedom of movement, yet it also reshaped our cities around traffic rather than people, contributed heavily to pollution and made many communities dependent on long commutes. It would be simplistic, however, to conclude that progress is therefore suspect. Medicine offers countless advances whose benefits are overwhelmingly clear. Ultimately, the question is not whether we should pursue progress, but whether we are sufficiently honest about its costs, and whether those who bear those costs have any say in the decision.

items.en: The Role of Art in Society
items.vi: Vai trò của nghệ thuật trong xã hội
items.p: Should governments fund the arts, even when there are more urgent needs such as healthcare and housing? Justify your position.
items.pv: Chính phủ có nên tài trợ nghệ thuật khi còn những nhu cầu cấp bách hơn như y tế, nhà ở? Lập luận cho quan điểm của bạn.
c: Lập luận giá trị của nghệ thuật
u: To dismiss the arts as a luxury is to
Coi nghệ thuật là xa xỉ tức là
Tôi sẵn sàng thừa nhận rằng
items.m: I would contend that governments should fund the arts, even in difficult times, although the scale and form of that funding deserve careful thought. To dismiss the arts as a luxury is to misunderstand their role. They are one of the principal ways in which a society reflects on itself, preserves its memory and imagines alternatives. They also have tangible benefits: cultural industries employ large numbers of people, and access to the arts has been linked to improved mental health and educational outcomes. I readily concede that when people lack adequate housing or medical care, those needs must take priority, and that arts funding can sometimes serve elite audiences rather than the public. What matters, then, is not whether to fund the arts, but how: prioritising projects that are genuinely accessible, rooted in communities and open to those who would otherwise be excluded.

items.vi: Quyền riêng tư thời số
items.p: "If you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear." Evaluate this argument about surveillance and privacy.
items.pv: “Không có gì để giấu thì chẳng có gì phải sợ.” Đánh giá lập luận này về giám sát và quyền riêng tư.
c: Nêu và diễn giải lập luận
Thừa nhận lý do giám sát
u: The argument has a superficial appeal, but
Lập luận nghe có lý bề ngoài, nhưng
It rests on the assumption that
Nó dựa trên giả định rằng
This is not to deny that
Điều này không phủ nhận rằng
items.m: The argument has a superficial appeal, but it collapses on closer inspection. It rests on the assumption that privacy matters only to people engaged in wrongdoing, which is plainly false. We close the bathroom door not because we are doing anything illegal, but because certain aspects of life are legitimately our own. Moreover, the argument assumes that those conducting surveillance will always be benevolent and competent, and that the definition of wrongdoing will never change. History suggests otherwise: information gathered for one purpose is frequently used for another. This is not to deny that some surveillance is justified, for example in investigating serious crime, provided it is targeted, proportionate and subject to independent oversight. In short, the question is not whether we have something to hide, but who decides what we must reveal, and with what safeguards.

items.vi: Thành công và hạnh phúc
items.p: How far do you agree that modern societies confuse success with happiness? Draw on personal observation or wider examples.
items.pv: Bạn đồng ý tới đâu rằng xã hội hiện đại nhầm lẫn thành công với hạnh phúc? Dùng quan sát cá nhân hoặc ví dụ rộng hơn.
c: Biểu hiện của sự nhầm lẫn
u: I am broadly in agreement, with one qualification.
Tôi về cơ bản đồng ý, với một điểm dè dặt.
Sự nhầm lẫn này thể hiện ở
Ví dụ tôi từng quan sát thấy
Perhaps the more fruitful question is
Có lẽ câu hỏi đáng bàn hơn là
items.m: I am broadly in agreement, with one qualification. This confusion manifests itself in the way we measure lives: by salary, job title, property and, increasingly, by visibility on social media. These markers are easy to compare and easy to display, which makes them convenient stand-ins for something far harder to assess. I have observed, for instance, friends who achieved every goal their parents set for them and yet describe themselves as exhausted and strangely empty. Research on wellbeing tends to support this impression: beyond a modest level of income, relationships, autonomy and a sense of purpose matter considerably more than further gains in status. My qualification is that success and happiness are not opposites; meaningful achievement can be a profound source of satisfaction. Perhaps the more fruitful question is not whether to pursue success, but whose definition of it we are pursuing.

items.vi: Phỏng vấn xin việc cấp quản lý: câu hỏi khó

learn.t: Thank you for coming. Let's start with a difficult one: what's your greatest weakness?

learn.vi: Thừa nhận đôi khi ôm việc thay vì giao cho người khác
learn.t: I've sometimes found it hard to delegate. I tend to take on too much myself rather than trusting the team.
And what have you done about that?

learn.vi: Nói bạn đã áp dụng họp giao việc hằng tuần và kết quả tốt hơn
learn.t: I introduced weekly planning meetings where tasks are assigned openly, and the team's output actually improved.
Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager.

learn.vi: Kể đã phản đối ra mắt sản phẩm sớm, đưa dữ liệu, được chấp nhận lùi hai tuần
learn.t: I once argued against launching a product early. I presented test data showing serious bugs, and we agreed to delay by two weeks.

learn.vi: Nêu kinh nghiệm quản lý nhóm đa văn hoá và kết quả đo được

tests.t: Why are you leaving your current position?

tests.vi: Trả lời tích cực: tìm thử thách mới, không chê công ty cũ

tests.vi: Nói sẽ nói chuyện riêng để tìm nguyên nhân, đặt mục tiêu rõ

tests.vi: Nói khi đó sẽ cùng phòng nhân sự xem xét các bước chính thức
tests.t: Then I'd involve HR and follow the formal procedure, while keeping the process fair and documented.

items.vi: Thuyết phục hội đồng khu phố về một dự án

learn.t: The council has concerns about turning the car park into a community garden. Convince us.

learn.vi: Nêu lợi ích: không gian xanh, trẻ em có chỗ chơi, giảm nhiệt
learn.t: The garden would give families a green space, give children somewhere safe to play and help cool the neighbourhood.
But local shops depend on that parking.

learn.vi: Đề xuất giữ một nửa chỗ đỗ xe, chỉ chuyển một nửa thành vườn
learn.t: We could keep half the spaces for parking and convert only the other half.
And who would maintain it? We have no budget.

learn.vi: Nói cư dân sẽ tình nguyện chăm, đã có 60 người đăng ký
learn.t: Residents would maintain it as volunteers. Sixty people have already signed up.
Interesting. We'll consider a one-year trial.

learn.vi: Cảm ơn, đề nghị báo cáo kết quả sau 6 tháng
learn.t: Thank you. We'd be happy to report back after six months.

tests.t: Why should we close this street to cars on Sundays?

Residents worry about noise.

All right, we'll try it for three months.

tests.vi: Cảm ơn, hứa thu ý kiến cư dân
tests.t: Thank you. We'll collect residents' feedback throughout.
